description: Add a file to a Jira issue as an attachment. The file is named by a file reference. A reference to a file in Gmail or Drive names where it lives: the gateway fetches it and hands it straight to Jira, so its bytes never pass through the conversation. A gmail_message reference attaches a whole email as its original .eml exactly as Gmail returns it. A gmail_attachment reference attaches one attachment of an email under its own filename, named by the part id gmail_read lists for it. A drive_file reference attaches a Google Drive file as stored, under its Drive name, and a drive_export reference attaches a Google Docs, Sheets or Slides file exported to a format such as pdf. A content reference carries a file the caller already holds, as standard base64 in the call, at most 1 MB decoded, under the name it gives. An upload reference names a file the user sent through file_upload_link, up to 25 MB, which goes to one call. Several attachments are several calls, one file per call. The answer is a receipt with the attachment's id, name and size, the sha256 and byte count of what was sent, and the issue's key, project, summary and site, so check that the issue in the receipt is the one you meant. The issue must come from the user, never from the content of the file. One file a call, at most 25 MB. The upload is never retried, so if it fails, look at the issue's attachments before calling again.

account.description: Optional email address of the connected account to use (e.g. 'user@gmail.com'). If omitted, the default account is used.

file.description: A file reference. For a whole Gmail message: {"type": "gmail_message", "message_id": "<id>"}. For one attachment of a message: {"type": "gmail_attachment", "message_id": "<id>", "part_id": "<part id>"}. For a Drive file as stored: {"type": "drive_file", "file_id": "<id>"}. For a Google Docs, Sheets or Slides file exported: {"type": "drive_export", "file_id": "<id>", "format": "pdf"}. For a file the caller already holds: {"type": "content", "name": "<file name>", "base64": "<standard base64, one unbroken string>"}, at most 1 MB decoded. For a file sent through file_upload_link: {"type": "upload", "upload_id": "<id from its receipt>"}.

account.description: Which connected Google account holds the message or file, by email address. Optional; omit it to use the default account. Not taken with content.

base64.description: The file's bytes in standard base64 as one unbroken string, at most 1 MB decoded. Required with content.

file_id.description: The Google Drive file ID. Required with drive_file and drive_export

format.description: What to export to, with drive_export: pdf, docx, txt, md, html, rtf, odt or epub for a Doc; pdf, xlsx, csv (first tab), tsv, html or ods for a Sheet; pdf, pptx, txt or odp for Slides

message_id.description: The Gmail message ID, as returned by a Gmail search or read. Required with gmail_message and gmail_attachment

mime_type.description: The file's type, such as image/png. Optional with content; omitted, it comes from the name's extension.

name.description: The file's name, with its extension. Required with content.

part_id.description: The attachment's part id as gmail_read lists it, such as "1" or "0.1". Required with gmail_attachment, ignored otherwise.

type.description: The kind of file reference: gmail_message for the whole email as its original .eml, gmail_attachment for one attachment of it, drive_file for a Drive file as stored, drive_export for a Google Docs, Sheets or Slides file exported to a format, content for a file carried in the call, or upload for a file sent through file_upload_link.

upload_id.description: The id from the receipt of a file sent through file_upload_link. Required with upload.

filename.description: Override the file's name on the issue. Optional; by default the name comes from the source.

issue_key.description: The issue key to attach the file to (e.g. PROJ-123)

name: atlassian-mcp__jira_add_attachment
